Blademarches (Blademarches, B33)

Region (English scoring-table division): Escann.

In one sentence: Raise the Gleaming Blade again in southern Escann, make rulers face the sword trial, and restore the old kingdom through sword schools, frontier fortresses, and an elite army.

Story: high｜Mission-tree length: medium (25 direct missions)｜Mission-tree update: specific date unverified, local version v1.37.5.0｜Distinctiveness: high｜Prison factor: medium｜Early pressure: depends on the predecessor｜Expansion capacity: very high.

A Country Behind a Broken Blade

The Blademarches are not a kingdom that can still be selected directly in 1444. The formation text recounts that the old Marches trained warriors to guard Calindal, the Gleaming Blade; when orc armies invaded during the Greentide, the knights fought to defend the holy sword, which was eventually broken, and the country fell with it. The long English offline Wiki entry adds earlier kingdom, Castanorian frontier, and chivalric-era context, and confirms that it was one of the last countries to fall during the Greentide. These belong to pre-1444 history, not to the player starting with an intact holy sword.【Local formation text】【Wiki source】

The modern Blademarches must be rebuilt in southern Escann. The current script does not restrict the entry to one specific adventurer company: the founder must hold the relevant area and key provinces, meet administrative-technology, peace, and ruler-ability or personality conditions, and then use the decision to become B33. If the predecessor is not a monarchy, it also changes to the Blademarches Kingdom reform. An old player post's claim that a southern adventurer is mandatory is a version- or experience-based summary and does not override the current decision.【Local script】【Community view】

The Crown Is a Sword Examination

The Blademarches' defining feature is not merely “high military bonuses,” but who is worthy to wield the sword. A dedicated event grants Calindal after formation, and the ruler or heir must face the Test of the Gleaming Blade; they may attempt it directly, nominate a wielder, or train the ruler. Training affects military ability, but failure may also occur, trigger a revolt, or require worthiness to be proved again. This cycle turns succession, ruler personality, and national legitimacy into an actual mechanic: an unfit heir is not merely a ruler with a few fewer monarch points, but a possible threat to the Blademarches' central political myth.【Local script】

Government reform further strengthens land-leader shock, army tradition, and monarch military ability; the national ideas emphasize morale, infantry, cavalry, discipline, and manpower. Its “blade” is not only a magical weapon, but also an officer school, a standard for choosing kings, and an army able to advance along the frontier. For players who enjoy an elite military state, that offers more immersion than an ordinary claim tree.【Local script】

From Southern Frontier to Empire of the Blade

The 25 direct B33 missions divide the restoration into several interlocking campaigns: recover the old lands and the Vernham school of swordsmanship, hold Dostan's Way, advance toward Marrhold and Trialmount, and prepare to enter the Deepwoods. Schools, roads, memorials, and steward strongholds anchor military expansion in specific regions. The final missions can grant permanent modifiers and overwrite the displayed country name as “Empire of the Blade,” but the Tag remains B33; no second imperial mission tree has been confirmed.【Local script】

The official Dev Diary 16 already described it in 2021 as a military restoration route, with goals including unifying Escann and entering the Deepwoods. The diary establishes that design direction; the current 25 missions and formation conditions still follow the local files. The Wiki also records a later setting line in which Stalbor rebuilds the Blademarches. That coexists with the script's multiple possible founders and cannot be used to cancel the player's other entry routes.【Official Dev Diary】【Wiki source】【Local script】

Playstyle and Personality

In the early game, any qualified predecessor must secure a foothold in the south; in the middle game, form B33 and manage the sword trial and succession; in the late game, build the officer system and frontier infrastructure while pursuing regional hegemony. Old player posts discuss founders and military strength; one AAR explicitly used save editing and reloading, so it demonstrates player-perceived appeal rather than base-game rules.【Local script】【Community view】

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 94/100｜Autocracy 85/100｜Magic↔Artifice 59/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 52/100)｜Pluralism 46/100.

The v2.1 values result is Neutral (58/100), with a mixed trajectory.

It suits players who like knightly restoration, heir development, and a high-quality army; players seeking a non-military route, peaceful construction, or clearly pluralist good governance may find its mission focus unappealing. Detailed formation thresholds, Wiki snapshots, and community version boundaries are recorded on the evidence page.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when the idea set is adopted, the seven ideas unlock in sequence as the idea group is filled, and the ambition applies after all seven ideas are unlocked. Only the national ideas themselves are listed; racial, government, and mission rewards are not mixed into the values. A new idea set after formation does not automatically stack with the old one. Idea descriptions may recall history or describe a future ideal and do not automatically mean that they had already happened in 1444.

Blademarches (B33) — Blademarcher Ideas

Traditions: Blademarcher Traditions

Effect: Army morale: +15%; Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Idea 1: Calindal, the Gleaming Blade

The Gleaming Blade was a greatsword used during the Dragonwake by Elecast Dragonsbane to slay the dragon Alos the Copper. While the blade is known for its sharp vorpal quality, it is most famous for the fact that, once drawn, it shines a light that is capable of blinding those who stare too close - this blinding nature of the blade has been used since time immemorial to determine the worthiness of the Blademarcher kings.

During the Decade of Masks it was discovered that the Gleaming Blade was none other than Calindal, a precursor spellblade named after and forged by the mythological elf-smith Calindal.

Effect: Land leader shock: +1; Monarch military skill: +1.

Idea 2: Revive the Bladestewards

The Order of the Bladestewards was a monastic order dedicated to protecting (Calindal, the Gleaming Blade) and ensuring that only the worthy may wield it and rule the Blademarches. Most members of the Blade Stewards are volunteers taken in by the Order, whether it be of unfortunate circumstance or simply a warrior looking for a higher cause. However, a small number of the Blade Stewards are known as Blind Masters, who are comprised of individuals who fail the test of the Gleaming Blade.

Effect: Army tradition: +0.5.

Idea 3: Legacy of the Dragonslayers

Elecast Dragonsbane, the founder of the kingdom, is the first ever-recorded dragonslayer in history. Our founder's renown is unmatched, and many respect our history and nation for it.

Effect: Diplomatic reputation: +100% (inherited display; unit conversion is unverified—see the English source-check note, rather than treating this as a verified percentage modifier).

Idea 4: Blade-Priests

By integrating our religion with the coronation of the monarch, we can strengthen both the devotion of our people to the faith and to the monarch.

Effect: Papal influence: +2; Yearly Corinite Paragonhood decay: raw value 0.1 (unit unverified); Church power modifier: +10%; Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Republican tradition: +0.3; Horde unity: +1.

Idea 5: Rise of the Bladechosen Kings

Calindal is Blademarch and Blademarch is Calindal. Any who wield the Gleaming Blade is a worthy ruler by default, and without them: we are nothing.

Effect: Yearly absolutism: +0.5; Maximum absolutism: +10.

Idea 6: Bright Hussars and Their Blinding Charge

A famous poem by Lord Wooley during the Fifth Blackpowder War, which details the last charge of the Blademarcher cavalry against a legion of mechanical soldiers:

"the last of the bright hussars came, with burning hearts and gleaming blade, onwards to mechanim death: fusillade, come powder's end: none remained."

-Lord Wooley (1853)

Effect: Cavalry combat ability: +15%.

Idea 7: Meritocracy at War and Peace Act

The Meritocracy at War and Peace Act was enacted in 1670 during the Witch-Kings Era which reformed the army and government as a whole, replacing all official positions to those of merit not feudal standing, gender or influence.

Effect: Female advisor chance: +50%; May recruit female generals: allowed; global_manpower_modifier: +15%.

Ambition: Blademarcher Ambition

Effect: Discipline: +5%.
